sentences.text: This appeal is preferred against the judgment and award dated 23rd August, 2019 passed in MVC No.350 of 2017 by the Senior Civil Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal at Kushtagi (for short hereinafter referred to as the "Tribunal").

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal at Kushtagi

NC: 2023:KHC-D:8928-DB Smt. Yallavva vs Ravutappa on 14 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/1471999/
2 2.
For the sake of convenience, the parties in these appeals are referred to with their status and rank before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are that on 20th January, 2017 when Yallappa was proceeding from Hungund to Ilkal on TVS vehicle on the left side of NH-50 in slow manner at 11.30 am, at that time near Fire Station the offending car bearing Registration No.KA-28/N-5222 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, dashed to the vehicle ridden by Yallappa and as a result, Yallappa sustained grievous injuries and died on the spot.
Accordingly, legal representatives of deceased-Yallappa filed claim petition seeking compensation for the reasons stated in the claim petition.
4. On service of notice, respondents 1 and 2 did not appear before the Court and were placed ex-parte.

Respondent No.3 appeared through his counsel and filed written statement contending that the driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid driving licence and one of the vehicle also violated policy conditions.

Further, he has denied all other averments NC:
2023:KHC-D:8928-DB made in the claim petition as false and sought for dismissal of the petition.
5. Based on the pleadings, the Tribunal framed five issues.
In order to prove their case, two witnesses were examined as PWs 1 and 2 on behalf of the petitioners and twenty documents were got marked as Exhibits P1 to P20.
Respondents have not adduced any evidence on their behalf.

6. On hearing arguments of both sides, the Tribunal has answered Issue No.1 in the affirmative;
issues 2 and 3 in the negative; and Issue No.4 partly in the affirmative and in view of the finding, the Tribunal has allowed the claim petition in part and awarded compensation of Rs.15,48,900/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realisation.
Being aggrieved by the impugned judgment and award, claimants have preferred this appeal for enhancement of compensation.
7. The learned counsel for the appellant has submitted his arguments that the Tribunal has not awarded the compensation in accordance with law and facts.

The Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased only at Rs.9,000/-
NC: 2023:KHC-D:8928-DB per month instead of Rs.30,000/- as claimed in the claim petition.
That there are six dependants, the Tribunal ought to have deducted one-fifth towards personal expenses of the deceased instead of one-fourth.
He further submits that the Tribunal has also not awarded compensation as per the decisions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court and on all these grounds, sought to allow the appeal.

8. Per contra, learned counsel appearing for the respondent-Insurance Company submitted that the Tribunal has awarded the compensation in accordance with law and there are no grounds to interfere with the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal and accordingly, sought for dismissal of the appeal.

3 9.

Having heard the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the parties, the following points would arise for our consideration in this appeal:
(1) Whether the appellants have made out ground for enhancement of compensation as sought for?
(2) What order or award?
NC: 2023:KHC-D:8928-DB 10.
We have carefully examined the material placed before us.
It is not in dispute that the deceased was an agriculturist and as per Exhibit P7-Postmortem report, the age of the deceased was 48 years.
The accident is of the year 2017.
The Tribunal has assessed the notional income of the deceased at Rs.9,000/- per month.
In consonance with the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, for the accidents of 2017, as per the chart, the notional income is Rs.10,250/-.
Accordingly the same is taken in this case also.

In view of the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED v. PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS reported in 2017 ACJ 2700, 25% of the income is to be added towards future prospects.

NC: 2023:KHC-D:8928-DB 12.

In the light of dictum of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED v. PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS reported in 2017 ACJ 2700, appellants are entitled for Rs.40,000/- each towards loss of consortium.
